subject: storytime
title: Goldilocks and the Bears
about: The tale of the girl who tries three bowls, three chairs and three beds in the bears' house, with a gentle ending: Goldilocks says sorry and learns to ask first. First graders know this story well, and the big, middle and little pattern makes every page easy to predict and read. It is a public-domain story retold here in first-grade words, five pages long.
tip: Ask him to retell it on three fingers: three bowls, three chairs, three beds, and what happened to each.

book.author: a folk tale (retold)
book.source: public domain, retold in first-grade words
book.blurb: Three bowls, three chairs, three beds and one sorry girl.

passage.text:
Three bears lived in a house in the woods.
There was a big Papa Bear.
There was a middle-sized Mama Bear.
And there was a wee little Baby Bear.
One morning, Mama Bear made porridge.
It was too hot to eat.
So the three bears went for a walk.
***
A girl named Goldilocks came by.
She peeked in the window.
No one was home.
So she went in.
She saw three bowls of porridge.
She tasted the big bowl.
"Too hot!"
She tasted the middle bowl.
"Too cold!"
She tasted the little bowl.
"Just right!"
And she ate it all up.
***
Then she saw three chairs.
The big chair was too hard.
The middle chair was too soft.
The little chair was just right.
Crack!
It broke.
Then she saw three beds.
The big bed was too hard.
The middle bed was too soft.
The little bed was just right.
Goldilocks fell fast asleep.
***
The three bears came home.
"Someone ate my porridge," said Papa Bear.
"Someone ate my porridge," said Mama Bear.
"Someone ate all of my porridge!" said Baby Bear.
"Someone sat in my chair," said Papa Bear.
"Someone broke my chair!" said Baby Bear.
"Someone slept in my bed," said Papa Bear.
"Someone is in my bed right now!" said Baby Bear.
***
Goldilocks woke up.
She saw the three bears.
"Oh my!" she said.
She jumped out of bed.
She ran all the way home.
"I am sorry," she said to her mom.
"That house was not mine."
Ask before you use what is not yours.

cards.q: Who lived in the house in the woods?
cards.note: Papa Bear, Mama Bear and Baby Bear: big, middle and little.
The setting is where a story happens; this one is a house in the woods.

cards.q: What did Goldilocks do with Baby Bear's porridge?
cards.note: Too hot, too cold, just right, and then it was gone.

cards.q: What happened to the little chair?
cards.note: Crack! It was just right, until it was not.

cards.q: What happened first in the story?
cards.note: The hot porridge is why the bears went out, and that is why the house was empty.

cards.q: What happened at the end of the story?
cards.note: She ran home and said sorry to her mom.

cards.q: How did Goldilocks feel when she saw the three bears?
cards.note: Oh my! Ask how the bears felt too, coming home to a stranger in a bed.
Ask before you use what is not yours; the last line says it.

cards.q: In the story, what does 'wee' mean?
cards.note: Wee is an old word for tiny; Baby Bear is the wee one.

cards.q: Which word is in the story?
cards.note: He reads the three words himself; only one of them is in the story.
